behaviour: plumb stores every record as a Markdown file with YAML frontmatter, identified by its frontmatter id, with bad or duplicate ids reported.
A record's hash ignores formatting and derived content and changes only when its meaning changes.
Links pin the hash of both ends, so a moved end makes the link stale and a missing target is an error.
An approval pins exact record content, so a later edit leaves the record unconfirmed and a requirement is covered only when every example has a test.
Only the owner's own explicit command or button confirms a record; the agent's reading or relay of the owner's words never does.
Log entries are append-only hash-chained files, and validate reports tampering.
Commit SR: trailers name the requirements served and are checked against the paths those requirements declare.
The merge boundary exits 4 while any touched requirement is unconfirmed and lists every approval in the range.
note: Overlaps SR-047, which wraps validate --merge as merge-check.

behaviour: The session brief is a short intent summary of about 30 lines that names records without carrying procedure.
note: Names SR-032 for the compact default; this holds the full brief.

behaviour: The prompt hook flags a prompt that contradicts or extends a confirmed requirement through the judge, and flags nothing by rule without one.
note: SR-038 restates the intent-change flag with its scoring against confirmed examples.

behaviour: The post-edit hook records edited paths for the session and never blocks the agent's tool call.
What needs the owner at the end of a turn reaches them as read-back or choice cards, raised only for real intent changes, unsettled records or regressions.
note: Refers to later SR-129/SR-134 card shapes; may be restated there.

behaviour: The status line prints one line from the session status file without loading records or running tests.
Each hook finishes within its time budget and never blocks work when plumb itself fails.
The installer sets up hooks, status line, deny rules, skill, CLAUDE.md block and commit hook, and running it twice changes nothing.
plumb builds a grep-able test map from requirements and source files to the tests that cover them.
For the files changed in a turn, plumb selects covering tests within a time budget and defers to full verification when coverage is shared or unknown.
Test evidence is pinned to tree, import closure, test source and environment, and reused only on an exact match.
A test that fails then passes on a same-tree rerun is recorded as flaky, not as a pass or regression.
A regression is a previously passing test that now fails, while a new test that starts red is exempt.
Judgment is advisory and uses the configured judge only; when none works plumb raises a named error with no heuristic fallback.
note: Restated in SR-038 and SR-044 as no-heuristic rule; INT-029 anchors it.

behaviour: plumb fidelity builds a scoped packet of a requirement, its code, tests and evidence so the host agent can judge it without JEV.
The importer reads pi-agent-factory read-only and imports every record as proposed unless upstream consent already pins its content.
note: Importer from an external register; may be one-off migration tooling.

behaviour: A judgment below the accept threshold is escalated to the host agent with a one-line instruction and its packet.
plumb init adopts any repository by creating .plumb/ idempotently.
A changed source path that no requirement owns is read back to the owner and a proposed requirement is recorded for it, without blocking.
A requirement whose acceptance test last failed is listed with its examples, and a regression of a touched requirement holds the merge with exit 5.
A requirement widened by a new owning link, or an exempted path, goes to the owner at the merge as an extension.
One shared definition of source code drives the untraced-change trace and covering-test selection, including flat layouts.
A confirmed example's acceptance test cannot change unseen: a changed verified_by end makes the requirement an unconfirmed edit that waits for the owner.
The merge is never green while an acceptance test the change can affect lacks a passing run on the current identity.
Hooks inject only records relevant and new to the session, pulling details on demand rather than resending them each prompt.
plumb explain answers in the owner's terms for plain words, a path or an ID, printing each record's upward chain.
plumb capture writes a whole read-back as proposed INT, SR and DEC records with pinned links in one call.
plumb new, intent, example and decide each write one proposed record, and decisions keep their alternatives and change only by a superseding decision.
plumb suggests an up-front spec once, in one line, when a request crosses stated size or risk triggers.
An escalated spec is an INT with members that the owner approves by one set-hash approval that the agent cannot record.
The intent-change flag scores a request against matched confirmed examples through the judge and flags only contradiction or extension.
The JEV client sits behind the judgment protocol, and its credential is named in config and read from the environment, never the repository.
plumb triage groups proposed records by the judge's faithfulness verdict so the owner confirms the low-risk group in one step.
Auto-approval is off by default, owner-switched and calibrated, and applies only to records restating the owner's own words.
plumb jev calibrate measures the judge against the owner's own decisions before any auto-approval is allowed.
The plumb-clarify skill scales clarification depth to the request and asks, in the question tool, only questions whose answers change what is built.
For an untraced change the judge proposes the owning requirement among code-map candidates, never writing a link.
A bounded scan proposes records that may silently depend on a changed record as drift hints, never as staleness or interruptions.
The agent may never decide the owner approved; confirmation comes only from the owner's typed command, a button press, or the reader of the owner's own message.
note: SR-005 states the same rule that the agent never decides the owner approved.

behaviour: plumb merge-check puts every unconfirmed touched requirement to the owner in one question and lists approvals the owner did not type.
merge-check runs the full suite at most once per invocation and reuses a passing run on an identical tree and environment.
